summary: RoadMesh backend API tested comprehensively. All 19 pytest tests PASSED (100%) covering auth (register+seed, duplicate, login, me, JWT), multi-tenant isolation (workshops A/B cannot access each other's clients/vehicles/photos), dashboard KPIs+enrichment, full CRUD for clients/vehicles/products, work-orders (totals compute correctly, stock discount + stock_movement logging, completed_at on status=concluido), purchase-orders (create pending + receive increments stock), quotes lifecycle (rascunho -> aceite -> convert only when aceite), photos (tenant-scoped via vehicle ownership), invoices (document_number ORC/FT/FR + year + counter, totals from work order). Portugal ISO dates and float pricing confirmed in responses. Backend implementation is solid.

minor.issue: Emails are lowercased server-side which is correct, but response returns lowercase even when user typed mixed-case — this is expected/correct behavior; noting for frontend to display accordingly.

When called without vehicle_id, returns photos across ALL workshops (no tenant filter applied to unfiltered query). Only vehicle_id path is tenant-guarded. Consider adding workshop_id filter unconditionally.
Same as /photos: no workshop_id filter on the base query, only vehicle_id-based safety. Should include tenant_filter unconditionally.
product stock update uses tenant_filter (good) but if a product no longer belongs to workshop (deleted), the stock_movement is still logged silently. Non-blocking.
Item number generation uses count_documents which is not concurrency-safe; two concurrent creates could yield the same #1024. Consider atomic counter. Non-blocking for MVP.
document_number counter is also count-based per (workshop, document_type); same concurrency caveat.

action_items: (Low priority) Add unconditional workshop_id filter to GET /api/photos and GET /api/damages base queries when vehicle_id is not passed, to prevent cross-tenant listing if the endpoints are ever called without vehicle_id.
(Optional) Replace count_documents-based numbering (work order #1024+n, invoice document_number, quote number) with an atomic MongoDB findAndModify counter to be concurrency-safe.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is a single 916-line file; consider splitting into routers (auth, clients, vehicles, work_orders, products, quotes, invoices, photos, dashboard) once the project grows.
JWT_SECRET falls back to a hardcoded default if env var missing; safer to fail fast (raise) if not set in production.
All models properly use uuid strings, no ObjectId leakage detected in responses (all queries use projection {'_id': 0}). Good.
Pydantic input validation is applied via typed models on all mutating endpoints. Good.
compute_totals correctly rounds to 2 decimals. Work-order totals verified (80 subtotal + 18.40 VAT = 98.40).
seed_data_creation: Registered two ephemeral TEST_ workshops via /api/auth/register (auto-seeded 5 clients + 5 vehicles + 5 products + 4 work orders + 1 invoice each). Test-created clients/vehicles/products/photos are prefixed TEST_ and cleaned up in-line where practical. Ephemeral workshops remain in DB but are isolated and harmless.
